tasks.title: Number the radios
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 1` in `kit_check.py`, print one line for each radio, numbered from 1 up to the number in `radios`. With 3 radios the lines are:

```
Radio 1 checked
Radio 2 checked
Radio 3 checked
```

Check runs your file with other numbers of radios, none included, and reads the lines that start with `Radio` among the lines Task 1 prints.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on `range`.
Work out which numbers the loop needs: where it starts and where it stops.
Write a `for` loop over a `range`, with one `print` moved in under it.
Run the file, then change `radios` at the top and run it again.
hints: One loop, one line per round. The loop's own name holds the number of the radio on each round.
`range(n)` gives 0, 1 and so on up to n - 1. Give it a start as well, and remember that it stops just before the number it is given.
The shape is `for number in range(1, ...):` with the number of radios plus one in place of the dots, and `print("Radio", number, "checked")` under it.

tasks.title: Rope for the lower
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 2`, make a variable called `total_rope`: the metres of rope for every pitch of the lower together. There are `pitches` pitches. The first is `first_pitch` metres long, and each pitch after it is `longer_by` metres longer than the one before. With 3 pitches, a first pitch of 10 and 10 longer each time, that is 10 + 20 + 30. Print it to see it.

Check runs your file with other pitches and reads `total_rope` after the lines under `# Task 2`.
nextSteps: Work out tonight's rope by hand first, pitch by pitch.
Start a total at 0 before the loop.
Loop once per pitch: add the pitch to the total, then make the next pitch longer.
Print the total after the loop and compare it with your sum by hand.
hints: This is a running total: a number that starts before the loop and grows on every round.

Two things change on each round: the total, and the length of the pitch. Keep the length in its own variable, starting at `first_pitch`. A total that starts inside the loop starts again on every round.
The shape is `total_rope = 0`, `pitch = first_pitch`, then `for count in range(pitches):` with `total_rope = total_rope + pitch` and `pitch = pitch + longer_by` under it.

tasks.title: Spell the stencils
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 3`, print each letter of `stretcher_label` on its own line, in capitals, and skip the spaces. For the label `Hill kit` the lines are:

```
H
I
L
L
K
I
T
```

Check runs your file with other labels and compares every line Task 3 prints with the letters, in order.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson on going through text letter by letter.
Inside the loop, print the letter in capitals only when it is not a space.
Run the file and read the letters down the terminal.
hints: A `for` loop over a text gives you one letter on each round, spaces included.
An `if` inside the loop can skip the spaces: a space is the text `" "`. The method that gives capitals comes from the lesson on text.
The shape is `for letter in stretcher_label:`, then `if letter != " ":` moved in under it, and `print(letter.upper())` moved in under that.

tasks.title: Count the stencils
tasks.description:
Under `# Task 4`, make a variable called `stencils`: how many letters `stretcher_label` has, not counting the spaces. For `Hill kit` that is 7. Print it to see it.

Check runs your file with other labels, one with several spaces among them, and reads `stencils` after the lines under `# Task 4`.
nextSteps: Look at your loop from Task 3: it visits every letter already.
Start a count at 0 before a loop of its own.
Add 1 to it for each letter that is not a space.
Print it after the loop and count one label by hand to compare.
hints: Counting is a running total that grows by 1.
`len` counts the spaces too, so it gives too many. A count that starts inside the loop starts again on every round.
The shape is `stencils = 0`, then `for letter in stretcher_label:` with `if letter != " ":` under it and `stencils = stencils + 1` under that.
